intro.title: useWindowSize
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Angular hook called `useWindowSize` that tracks the current width and height of the browser window. You will learn how to use the `window` object to listen for resize events and update component state accordingly. The main technologies involved are Angular's `OnInit` and `OnDestroy` lifecycle hooks, RxJS for handling events, and TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that dynamically responds to window size changes, enhancing your understanding of reactive state management in Angular.
intro.usecase: The useWindowSize pattern is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes in real-time. In dashboard applications, developers use window size detection to rearrange charts, tables, and widgets when users resize their browser or switch between desktop and tablet modes. E-commerce sites implement this to adjust product grids, navigation menus, and image galleries dynamically. Media players and data visualization tools rely on window size tracking to optimize layout and maintain usability across devices, ensuring content remains accessible and visually balanced regardless of viewport changes.
